title: Page-mode body text center taps can miss reader chrome toggle
symptom: In page mode, tapping the center of real body text on a later page can leave the reader in immersive mode with only the compact header visible, while right-edge taps still turn pages. The issue was reproduced with a real imported TXT sample and with an instrumentation regression that executes shell-level `input tap` on body text.
root_cause: The page tap-zone handler lived outside the HorizontalPager/page gesture path, so taps landing on body Text content were not reliably observed after the pager consumed pointer events. UiDevice clicks could pass while lower-level shell taps still missed, hiding the real interaction gap.
fix: Move page tap-zone observation onto the HorizontalPager modifier so it participates in the pager gesture path.

Observe pointer events with `awaitFirstDown(requireUnconsumed = false)` and read the final up event after parent consumption, while ignoring movements beyond touch slop so swipes are not treated as taps.
Add a later-page body-text regression that executes shell-level `input tap` and asserts the reader top bar and bottom controls appear.
failed_attempts: Do not rely only on UiDevice.click regressions; they can pass while shell-level or real lower-level taps still miss the chrome toggle.
Do not attach a normal `detectTapGestures` handler inside the page surface; it can still lose events to the pager's scrollable gesture handling.
Do not treat static screenshots alone as proof for this bug; the failure depends on a specific tap delivery path after page navigation.

When refactoring page-mode pointerInput handling, avoid routing stable taps through a local function reference such as `?.let(::handlePageTap)`. On Pixel 8 / Android 14 this caused ReaderPageModeTest cross-chapter right-tap paths to miss the final chapter switch, while the equivalent explicit `if (tapZone != null) handlePageTap(tapZone)` path passed.
impact: Users could be trapped in immersive reading on dense real TXT pages unless they found a blank area or used another gesture, making settings, TOC, and TTS controls feel intermittently unavailable.
